Usually, works of literature don't openly state their themes. But you can often identify themes by looking at important moments in the text, including dialogue, action, and observations made by the narrator.

—Natalie Babbitt, Tuck Everlasting. © 1975

The narrator's mother is willing to give up her time for her child.

contents.text: When you leave something alone, you stop bothering it and go away. Let means to allow; to give someone permission.

header.text: This is the correct text:

contents.text: Snakes will usually not harm you if you leave them alone and keep a safe distance from them.

header.text: Fix the one word that is used incorrectly.

contents.text: Certain words are often confused with one another. In your writing, you should pay close attention to these words and make sure you are using them correctly.

header.text: For example, fewer and less have similar meanings, but you should use them differently. Use fewer to describe things you can count, like pencils. Use less to describe things you can't count, like water.

contents.text: Fewer people than expected came to watch the race.
Our town received less snow this winter due to the heat wave.

header.text: Affect and effect have similar spellings and can sound the same, but they have different meanings. Affect is usually a verb that means to change or influence. Effect is usually a noun that means an outcome or result.

contents.text: Our team was losing, but I tried not to let that affect my performance.
The new medicine has an amazing effect on cold symptoms.

header.text: Fix the one word that is used incorrectly.
Dessert should be changed to desert.

contents.text: A desert is a dry region often with little to no vegetation. A dessert is a sweet food often eaten at the end of a meal.

contents.text: Antarctica is the world's largest desert. On average it receives only 6.5 inches of precipitation every year.
